blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:intro label="sec:intro"}

In this work, we present quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) calculations, including both variational Monte Carlo (VMC) and Green's Function Monte Carlo (GFMC) methods, to study magnetic moments and form factors of $A\le 10$ nuclei. We use the precise experimental measurements of these electromagnetic observables to validate our microscopic modeling; namely, we verify the accuracy of the approach in which we treat the nucleus as a system of correlated nucleons interacting amongst themselves via two- and three-nucleon forces. The Norfolk interaction model
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:nv23 label="sec:nv23"}

We base our calculations on electromagnetic many-body currents [@Pastore:2008ui; @Pastore:2009is; @Schiavilla:2018udt; @Gnech:2022vwr] derived consistently with the Norfolk two- and three-body (NV2+3) nuclear interactions [@Piarulli:2014bda; @Piarulli:2016vel; @Piarulli:2017dwd; @Baroni:2018fdn; @Piarulli:2019cqu]. The Norfolk two-body potential (NV2) is a fully local interaction -- hence suitable to be utilized within QMC methods -- and includes terms up to N3LO in the $\chi$EFT expansion. Results and Discussion
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:results label="sec:results"}

In this section, we summarize our calculations. Specifically, we report the results for i) magnetic moments; ii) two-body magnetic densities; and iii) magnetic form factors of light nuclei.

blocks.title: Lithium-6
blocks.content: The ${}^6\text{Li}$ experimental magnetic form factor presents two peaks at $q\simeq0.5$ and 2 fm$^{-1}$ [@Peterson1962; @Goldemberg1963; @Rand1966; @Lapikas1978; @Bergstrom1982]. Our calculations are able to reproduce the two peaks even if, for all the interactions considered, the zero tends to come a little too early, and the second peak contains too much strength. This is evidenced when comparing the theoretical error bands with the experimental data in Fig. [\[fig:MFF_err\]](#fig:MFF_err){reference-type="ref" reference="fig:MFF_err"}c. blocks.content: The ${}^7\text{Li}$ and ${}^7\text{Be}$ magnetic f.f.'s receive contributions from $M_1$ and $M_3$ multipoles, as can be seen in Figs. [\[fig:MFF_multipole_IIb\]](#fig:MFF_multipole_IIb){reference-type="ref" reference="fig:MFF_multipole_IIb"}a and [\[fig:MFF_multipole_IIb\]](#fig:MFF_multipole_IIb){reference-type="ref" reference="fig:MFF_multipole_IIb"}b. blocks.title: Lithium-8 and Boron-8
blocks.content: There are no experimental data for the magnetic f.f.'s of the $A=8$ systems; however, from our calculations, we observe again a large contribution from two-body currents (Figs. [\[fig:MFF_IIb_co\]](#fig:MFF_IIb_co){reference-type="ref" reference="fig:MFF_IIb_co"}, panels (f) and (g)). This is particularly striking in $^8$B, where two-body currents reduce the strength of the form factor for all $q$. blocks.title: Boron-10
blocks.content: The experimental data for the ${}^{10}\text{B}$ magnetic f.f. are provided for $0.5\lesssim q \lesssim 2.0$ fm$^{-1}$ region [@Goldemberg1963; @Goldemberg1965; @Rand1966; @Vanpraet1965; @Lapikas1978]. We did not include the data of Refs. [@Goldemberg1963; @Goldemberg1965] in the plots because of the strong disagreement with the more recent experimental results reported in Ref. [@Donnelly1984]. The VMC calculation has a very nice agreement with the data in the region of the main peak (see Fig. [\[fig:MFF_IIb_co\]](#fig:MFF_IIb_co){reference-type="ref" reference="fig:MFF_IIb_co"}l). blocks.title: Conclusions
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:conclusion label="sec:conclusion"} In this work we presented QMC calculations of magnetic moments and magnetic form factors of nuclei for $A\leq10$ based on chiral effective field theory. For the calculation we used the Norfolk two- and three- body interaction and consistent one- and two-body current operators.
